summary: Iteration 4: 41/41 backend tests PASS. Verified admin JWT auth (login OK with 'Rithi0518@', 401 on wrong pw, 429 rate-limit after many bad attempts, /auth/me works with Bearer, change-password + restore round-trip). All admin endpoints (dashboard/stats, notifications, painel, customers, templates, settings, payments, messages, whatsapp/status, trials) correctly return 401 without token and 200 with token. Public endpoints (/api/, /api/health, /api/pay/customer/*, /api/whatsapp/incoming, /api/public/trial, /api/uploads/{filename}) work WITHOUT auth. Uploads: POST /api/uploads accepts png (returns url/path/filename/size), rejects .txt with 400, requires auth (401 without), GET /api/uploads/{fname} public. Notifications now returns 9 templates including expiration_7d + expired_1d/3d/7d. Painel /users returns cached shape (users,count,cache_updated_at,refreshing,last_error) quickly; /users/refresh returns 200 with success:false + error (Cloudflare 403 expected). Regression: all iteration 2/3 flows still pass (customers CRUD, templates trigger_source, settings R$ prices, payments prices_cents, whatsapp incoming save, package-ids, renew 502). Admin password restored to original.

minor.issue: Rate-limit is in-memory per worker process. With multiple backend workers/replicas, an attacker gets 8*N attempts before hard-block. Not a blocker for MVP but consider moving to shared store (redis/sqlite) if production traffic grows.
Real painel.fun refresh fails with Cloudflare 403 in datacenter — expected. Response shape {success:false, error:'...'} is correct.

critical_code_review_comments: services/auth.py — JWT_SECRET default fallback 'insecure-default-please-change' is safe since .env sets it, but consider raising on missing env in prod build.
routers/auth.py — brute-force map _failed is in-memory dict, per-worker; will not persist across restarts nor across replicas. Fine for single-instance Raspberry deployment but flag if scaling out.
routers/uploads.py — URL is built from request.headers x-forwarded-proto/host; if header spoofing is a concern, prefer configured PUBLIC_BASE_URL from settings.

services/auth.py is_public — /api/pay/customer/ is public which exposes prices+customer info by ID; acceptable for a shareable pay link but ensure IDs are non-guessable (UUIDs) — verified via customers router (uses uuid).
server.py auth middleware calls require_admin(request) as a plain awaitable rather than a FastAPI dependency — works because require_admin is a regular async function that takes Request. OK.
